about: MUTATING — deletes the copy of Forgejo's data that move-forgejo-data left on the forge's root filesystem, /opt/forgejo/data.pre-move-<8 hex> (infra/forge/move-forgejo-data.sh --delete; backlog 192a9003, the follow-on of 016aeea3). The move renames the old copy aside as its commit point and leaves it for its rollback, so the root disk — whose space is the whole point, alarm c4da71b0 — gets nothing back until it is deleted, and until this verb nothing could delete it. In design 17835005's shape and authorised per run by David's passkey: it declares requires_approval with plan-a-forgejo-premove-delete as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders the plan with the command --plan-delete uses and changes nothing unless the bytes hash alike, so a copy that changed after the signature is refused. It takes no path: what it deletes is derived the way the move derived its rename target, and it refuses (exit 78, nothing changed) unless Forgejo runs, its healthz passes, the container's /data is the moved copy by device and inode and not the copy to delete, the repository it serves is the moved copy's, the registry serves the converge's current stamp, /opt/forgejo/data is mounted as exactly the move's bind with the move's fstab line and the drive's by-UUID line, the move's served marker is a move's record at least 24 hours old (the rollback window — a day of pushes, trains and registry pulls served off the new drive), no move or rollback run still holds the converge, and exactly one copy matches: a real directory on /, not a mount, nothing mounted beneath it, mounted by no running container and held by no host process. The act: rename the copy to /opt/forgejo/data.deleting-<8 hex> (atomic, so from then on no rollback plan finds a pre-move copy and a copy half deleted is never put back), rm -rf --one-file-system that name, confirm it is gone, prove / has grown by the copy's measured size less a slack (the larger of a tenth and 2 GiB, re-read while ext4 settles), and read the proof again. It never stops, starts or holds anything, and touches no other path. A failure after the rename is exit 1 with what stands printed; a remainder left by an interrupted run is finished by rendering plan-a-forgejo-premove-delete again. After it, roll-back-forgejo-data-move has no copy to put back, and the plan says so.
